10. It is further argued that the courts below failed to find that the defendants could not submit any document before the trial court showing that Azahar Ali Mridha obtained settlement of the property from Rezia Khatun by any deed of settlement, kubaliyat or rent receipt and could not show the basis of SA khatian in any manner, but the courts below on an speculation observed that somehow Azahar Ali Mridha obtained the property by way of pattan, consequently, SA khatian recorded in his name which has no basis at all. 

 15. Mr. Omit Roy, Advocate with Mr. Kawser Rahman Kafi, learned Advocates appearing for the opposite parties submit that admittedly the suit property belonged to Rezia Khatun by purchase, from whom predecessor of defendants named Azahar Ali Mridha obtained pattan by way of payment of rents and obtaining rent receipts, but said rent receipt (চেক দাখিল) could not be filed before the trial court as those dakhilas were not taken return from the office of the Settlement Officer, where Azahar Ali Mridha submitted those dakhilas before hearing of objection case and appeal case. 

 25. Learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the defendants could not produce any document showing their settlement from Rezia Khatun before the trial court, as such, SA record has no basis. From perusal of exhibit-Umo-3, it appears that Appeal Officer in his judgment observed that Azahar Ali Mridha claimed that he obtained pattan from Rezia Khatun before the SAT Act came into force and he executed a kabuliyat before delivery of possession and after obtaining settlement he constructed homestead thereon and living with his family members, but Azahar Ali Mridha could not file kabuliyat before the Settlement Officer and Appeal Officer, however, he produced rent receipts showing payment of rent to Rezia Khatun and after SAT Act came into force he regularly made payment of rents to the government. 

 29. It is also true that mere payment of rents to the government by a person having no title in the property on the basis of wrong record-of-right does not create title in his favour unless he could show the basis of record-of-right, but the facts and circumstances of this case is totally different from the cases cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioners reported in 56 DLR and 10 MLR. All the decisions referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioners did not match with the facts and circumstances of the present case. Therefore, the trial court as well as the appellate court concurrently observed that the plaintiffs in suit failed to prove their title and possession in the suit property. On the other hand, the defendants by oral evidence, series of exhibits could able to prove that Azahar Ali Mridha acquired the suit property by way of pattan from Rezia Khatun and Rezia Khatun fought against Azahar Ali Mridha but failed. Where original owner Rezia Khatun gave up the claim during her life time conceding title and possession of Azahar Ali Mridha, her heirs, subsequently, after about two decades cannot come with the present suit claiming that they inherited the property from Rezia Khatun who purchased the same in the year 1944 and 1945.
